extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), USPTO disciplinary counsel, and parties to USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures the USPTO applies when evaluating alleged professional misconduct by patent practitioners, especially conflicts of interest and inventorship disputes, and the sanctions and mitigation factors considered in settlement. Covers which rules apply (pre-/post-changeover), jurisdictional authority, and corrective/disciplinary remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction to discipline practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings against registered patent practitioners are brought and decided under the cited statutory and regulatory authority; disciplinary settlements are submitted to the USPTO Director for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing professional conduct rules by date
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq., applies to alleged misconduct that occurred prior to May 3, 2013. The USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq., apply to alleged misconduct occurring after May 2, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which version of the USPTO professional conduct rules governs based on the date(s) of the alleged misconduct when evaluating or charging practitioner conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple employment/conflict: 37 C.F.R. § 10.66(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not continue multiple employment if the exercise of the practitioner's independent professional judgment on behalf of the client will be or is likely to be adversely affected by the practitioner's representation of another client, or if it would be likely to involve the practitioner in representing differing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing to represent multiple clients where independent judgment is or likely will be impaired, without consent after full disclosure, violates § 10.66(b). Facts such as knowledge of a dispute and continuing joint representation despite that knowledge support a finding of violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent conflict rule: 37 C.F.R. § 11.107(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not represent a client if the representation of one client will be directly adverse to another, or where there is a significant risk that the representation of a client will be materially limited by the practitioner's responsibilities to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuing to represent co-inventors as joint clients when their interests are directly adverse (e.g., an inventorship dispute) is prohibited under § 11.107(a); material limitation is assessed by whether responsibilities to one client materially limit representation of the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Former-client conflict and written informed consent: 37 C.F.R. § 11.109(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who has formerly represented a client in a matter shall not thereafter represent another person in the same or a substantially related matter in which that person's interests are materially adverse to the interests of the former client unless the former client gives informed consent, confirmed in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a practitioner previously represented co-clients on the same invention, then representing one of them afterwards (when interests are materially adverse) requires the former client's informed consent, confirmed in writing; absence of such written consent supports a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When potential differing interests arise, the practitioner must obtain the client's consent after full disclosure of the possible effect of the representation on the exercise of the practitioner's independent professional judgment on the client's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full disclosure plus consent (and when required, written confirmation) is necessary to continue multiple or adverse representations; lack of disclosure or consent is a basis for discipline (as stated in paragraph admitting violation of § 10.66(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to keep clients informed of filings and communications affecting their interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must inform clients about significant filings and communications that affect the clients' rights or interests (e.g., abandonment of a parent application, filing of a continuation, or communications about inventorship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to advise a client that the practitioner filed an express abandonment and a continuation naming a different sole inventor, or failing to keep a client informed about communications regarding inventorship, is cited as problematic conduct supporting disciplinary action in this matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for resolving inventorship disputes (mediation/arbitration and formal correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to binding arbitration/mediation for an independent determination of inventorship, and, if appropriate, formalize the determination by filing a certificate of correction under 37 C.F.R. § 1.324.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempting to obtain an independent inventorship determination via mediation/arbitration and using § 1.324 to effectuate a correction is an identified approach; failure to obtain agreement from all parties limits this option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available and publication of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions include public reprimand and publication of the Final Order; the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and publish the Final Order in the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary settlements may specify public reprimand and require publication of the order and notice. The Office may also use the record in future proceedings as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations by the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating and aggravating factors considered in discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors considered in mitigation include length of practice (Respondent was a member of the patent bar for almost 50 years), absence of prior disciplinary history, and lack of dishonest or selfish motive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office weighs such mitigating factors when agreeing to or imposing sanctions; conversely, the record may be used as an aggravating factor in future proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and procedural disposition terms
rubrics_metrics.description: A settlement agreement can resolve disciplinary action and include terms such as dismissal of pending disciplinary proceedings (the OED Director to file a motion requesting dismissal within fourteen days), payment/ bearing of costs, and agreed sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary matters may be concluded by approved settlement agreements specifying sanctions, publication, dismissal motions, and allocation of costs; the Office reserves the right to consider the record in future matters.
